expectations.text: Output identifies 5 or more distinct domains affected
expectations.evidence: 7 distinct domains identified: Engineering Team, Hiring/Talent Pipeline, Customers/Transaction Processing, Vendor/Tooling Ecosystem, Finance/Budget, Regulatory/Compliance, Product Velocity/Competitive Position

expectations.text: Output traces at least 2 orders of effects beyond first-order for the majority of domains
expectations.evidence: All 7 domains have 1st, 2nd, and 3rd order effects with explicit order labels in table format

expectations.text: Output identifies at least 2 feedback loops with mechanism explanations
expectations.evidence: 4 feedback loops identified: Training Investment Poaching Spiral, Dual-Stack Maintenance Trap, Feature Drought Customer Loss Spiral, Incident Paradox. Each has detailed mechanism explanation

expectations.text: Output labels feedback loops as amplifying or dampening
expectations.evidence: Loops 1-3 labeled 'Amplifying (vicious)', Loop 4 labeled 'Dampening (self-correcting, virtuous)'. Each has Type field explicitly stated

expectations.text: Output is structured with clear domain-by-domain organization
expectations.evidence: Uses structured table format with Domain Analysis section containing 7 subsections, each with Order/Effect/Mechanism columns

expectations.text: Output includes at least 1 counter-intuitive or non-obvious effect
expectations.evidence: Multiple counter-intuitive effects: (1) 'Incident response degrades despite fewer bugs' in Vendor/Tooling domain, (2) 'better technology, worse outcomes' in Key Risks, (3) training investment subsidizing competitors in Hiring domain

expectations.text: Output provides mechanisms (why/because) for causal chains, not just listing effects
expectations.evidence: Every effect row has a Mechanism column with specific causal explanation. E.g., 'High performers have options and leave uncertain environments first (adverse selection)'
